sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020 [publ. 2021]. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-67. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any language. Table 1 (p. 48) 'Status of East Kainji languages' lists Vono (Western/Kauru subgroup) with '?' in both Status and Source columns, where '? signifies no information'; p. 47: 'Many languages, especially of the Western branch appear to have no material available at all.' The phonology section (3.1, pp. 54-58) describes only ɛBoze (four level tones plus glides; other East Kainji languages 'much reduced systems', tiMap two tones plus rising). Vono is absent from the data appendix (Table 12: 'Languages for which no data exists are not listed').

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1314323
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vono appears only as a node under 'Kaduna' in the East Kainji tree (Fig. 7, p. 83); no lexical or phonological data; nothing on stress.
